page: Microsoft Azure F16-8amds_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Famdsv7 server family. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at a dedicated clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The configuration includes 8 physical cores and 8 vCPUs, operating with a hypervisor-managed single thread per core. It features 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 16.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a 1890 GB NVMe SSD and is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core metrics and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression rates placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core CPU performance, passmark CPU metrics, and memory bandwidth fall within the average range. The server demonstrates strong performance in small-model LLM inference, achieving top-tier text generation speeds of 369.42 tokens per second for a 135M model. However, performance drops significantly for larger models, with prompt processing for a 70B model falling into the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F16-8amds_v7 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio combined with fast local NVMe storage, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel core scaling. The dedicated 4.5 GHz CPU cores provide strong single-threaded execution, though multi-threaded scaling remains average. This hardware profile is suited for database operations, memory-cached applications, and lightweight language model inference.
